abstract: Risk factors, their interrelationship, and prognostic relevance for seminoma stage II disease have been examined. The size of the primary tumor was significantly correlated with the pT category, as was the presence of tumor invasion of small vessels. The pT category was correlated neither with clinical substage nor relapse rate. There was a poorer 3-year survival for anaplastic seminomas as compared to that of classical seminomas; the difference was not significant. The 5-year survival for seminomas rich in lymphocytes was better than those of poor lymphocytic infiltration, but this difference also was not significant. No difference in survival or relapse rate was found between HCG-producing and HCG-nonproducing seminomas.
abstract_ja: 病期IIのセミノーマにおけるリスク因子、その相互関係、および予後的意義を検討した。原発腫瘍の大きさはpT分類と有意に相関し、小血管への腫瘍浸潤の有無も同様であった。pT分類は臨床病期の亜分類とも再発率とも相関しなかった。未分化型セミノーマは古典型セミノーマに比べ3年生存率が低かったが、その差は有意ではなかった。リンパ球浸潤が豊富なセミノーマの5年生存率は、リンパ球浸潤に乏しいものより良好であったが、この差も有意ではなかった。hCG産生セミノーマと非産生セミノーマの間で、生存率および再発率に差は認められなかった。
